intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The Fat Goose inn is fast asleep. But every night, strange sounds come from the cellar: rustling, clinking and a little giggle.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: My spoons are gone. So are my buttons, and my best frying pan! Somebody is taking everything that shines.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Go down and sort it out. But don't smash the barrels. That's my kvass in there.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Well, shall we go down?

variants.warden: Stay behind me. I go first, as always.
variants.wind-archer: Quiet. I hear tiny paws. Lots of tiny paws.
variants.herbalist: Rats? Good thing I packed my bite ointment.
variants.rogue: Cellars are my favorite part of town. After the rooftops.
variants.elementalist: My book says gremlins fear sparks. Let's find out!
variants.tinker: Bolt, sniff around. But don't bite anything rusty.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Off you go, then. I'll put the kettle on.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The rat squeaked, dropped its spoon and dashed into a crack. The fog drifted off it like smoke.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the wine cellar, a gremlin sits on a chest. On his head is Mistress Marta's frying pan, worn like a helmet.

lines.speaker: rogue
lines.text: A frying pan for a helmet? Bold. But I'm taking it back.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: Hello down there! I hear banging! I hope that's not my kvass.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: In the corner, under a heap of stolen spoons, something began to glow warmly.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: It's glowing!

variants.warden: Wow! It glows like a lantern at the fair.
variants.wind-archer: So warm. Like holding a bit of sunshine.
variants.herbalist: It smells of honey and light. A good sign.
variants.rogue: My find! Well, our find.
variants.elementalist: Incredible! May I hold it? I'll be careful!
variants.tinker: Fine work. Who broke you, poor thing?

victory.speaker: marta
victory.text: That's a piece of our Lantern! Those critters were hoarding it like treasure.

victory.speaker: marta
victory.text: I'll wrap it in a scarf. Something tells me this is only the beginning.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Hello, Bravehearts! Come up from the cellar before the rats take your boots too.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Have a snack, patch yourselves up, and we'll try again.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: The spoons are back, and so is the frying pan. It does have tiny tooth marks now.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Beyond the town begins Thornwood. The fog lies low here, like a cat sneaking up on a mouse.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The forester saw a light near the old lodge. The same glow as our lantern piece.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The path is short but prickly. Don't dawdle. Just head for the lodge.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Yellow eyes flash in the bushes. One pair, then another, then one more.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Someone's there!

variants.warden: Shields up! Something's out there!
variants.wind-archer: Movement in the bushes! Two. No, four.
variants.herbalist: Careful. Something is wrong here.
variants.rogue: Shh. Someone's there. And they're not very polite.
variants.elementalist: I feel magic. And I don't like it.
variants.tinker: Bolt is growling. Trouble is close.

lines.speaker: herbalist
lines.text: Thorns don't prick out of spite. Walk around the bushes and they'll leave you alone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ravine is narrow and dark. Something iron glints between the rocks. It looks like a trap.

lines.speaker: wind-archer
lines.text: I grew up in the mountains, near wolves. They aren't mean. They're just lost in the fog.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wolf shook its head as if waking up, and bounded into the woods. Without the fog, it is just a gray wolf again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A big fellow in a black and purple scarf guards the lodge. A bandit!

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The lodge was empty. Only ashes from a campfire, boot prints, and a scarf on a nail.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: On the table lay a map. A cross was marked on the old mill by the marsh.

victory.speaker: marta
victory.text: The mill? Good old Bruno the miller lives there. What would bandits want with him?

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Not all at once, Bravehearts. Even wolves don't find the path the first time.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Mend your cloaks, and I'll give you more ointment for the scratches.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: The forester sent a basket of mushrooms. He says the wolves are calm and polite again, just like before.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The river has burst its banks, and the old mill stands knee-deep in water. The wheel creaks, though nobody turns it.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Bandits guard the yard. And in the millpond under the wheel, something mumbles. Something big and wet.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: They say the sluice has a lever that lets the water out. Find it, and things get easier.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: We have to help Bruno.

variants.warden: Wet boots are no reason to turn back.
variants.wind-archer: Water hides our steps. Stay close.
variants.herbalist: Bruno always gave me bagels. We have to help him.
variants.rogue: Bandits in someone else's yard? Rude. I always ask permission. Sometimes.
variants.elementalist: So much water! Too bad I haven't learned to dry it up.
variants.tinker: A mill wheel is a machine. And I love rescuing machines.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Bog slimes bubble in the sluice. By the wall stands an old lever, covered in mud.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: The lever is fine, just rusty. Somebody go and give it a good pull!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wheel creaked and stopped. Slowly, the Bog Miller rises from the water.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: Who dared to stop my mill?! Did you come to take the light too?

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: My head hums like a millstone. Who are you? No, go away! The fog says you are enemies!

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Bruno, we're friends! Hang on!

variants.warden: Bruno, we're friends! Hang on, we'll pull you out.
variants.wind-archer: He's fighting the fog. Just a little more!
variants.herbalist: Bruno, it's me, the Herbalist! Remember my herbs and your bagels!
variants.rogue: Uncle Bruno, wake up! You're a good man, I know it.
variants.elementalist: The fog is losing its grip! I can feel it!
variants.tinker: Almost there. This mud will slide right off, like rust off a gear.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The mud slides off the Miller, and he is himself again: tired, kind Bruno.

victory.speaker: miller
victory.text: Oh, my head is like a millstone. How long was I asleep?

victory.speaker: herbalist
victory.text: Here, Bruno, a sip of mint tea. You'll feel new in an hour.

victory.speaker: miller
victory.text: I remember a tall man in a cloak made of shadow. On his chest hung a glass ball, and inside it was our light.

victory.speaker: miller
victory.text: He called himself Shadowhand. His men hauled crates to the old watchtower.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: That wet giant is still our Bruno, only muddled. Don't give up. He is waiting for you.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Dry your boots by the stove, and back to the mill you go.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: Bruno ate three bowls of soup and fell asleep right at the table. Let him sleep. He earned it.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Lights burn again in the tower above the pass. But this light is cold and purple.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Bruno says Shadowhand's cultists hid the second piece of the Lantern up there.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The door to the upper floor is locked. One of the cultists carries the key. Go and find it.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The runes on the walls flash, one after another. Stone sentinels open their eyes.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: They're awake!

variants.warden: Stone sentinels? Let's see which of us guards better.
variants.wind-archer: The wind smells of mountains. Almost like home.
variants.herbalist: I don't like these runes. Stay off the purple tiles.
variants.rogue: A tower, a locked door, and the key in someone else's pocket. Perfect evening.
variants.elementalist: Gloom runes! I saw them in a forbidden book. Well, I almost didn't read it.
variants.tinker: Stone sentinels are ancient automatons. Bolt, don't bark. They're nervous.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gloom cultists whisper in the barracks. Glowing rune circles surround them on the floor.

lines.speaker: elementalist
lines.text: These runes protect the cultists. Lure them out of the circles!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The blue spark in the sentinel's eyes went out. The stone is just stone again.

lines.speaker: warden
lines.text: Rest now, stone friend. Your watch is over.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The lock clicked. A shadow slipped up the stairs. Someone is already waiting on the upper floor.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The shadows in the tower grow thicker. Time to grab the light and head for the gate!

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The second piece of the Lantern is warm, like bread from the oven.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The two pieces fit together, as if they had always been waiting for each other. But without its heart, the Lantern cannot shine.

victory.speaker: marta
victory.text: And this black glass key opens a cave under the Gray Mountains. The old folks call it the Heart of Gloom.

victory.speaker: wind-archer
victory.text: The Gray Mountains are my home. I know the way.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: The tower is tall and the stairs are steep. Never mind. Next time you'll climb faster.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Just remember: the light must not only be found, but carried home.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: Tomorrow the whole town will see you off. The baker is already kneading bread for the road.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Under the Gray Mountains, behind a door of black glass, hides the Heart of Gloom.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Shadowhand keeps our light there. Dark braziers stand along the walls. Light them, and the shadow has nowhere to hide.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: And come back, all of you. I'll be counting you at the door.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Let's get our light back.

variants.warden: My shield was once the door of our town hall. Today it guards Alba again.
variants.wind-archer: I know these mountains. It was never this dark here.
variants.herbalist: I packed all my herbs. Even the ones that smell like socks.
variants.rogue: Stealing a whole town's light? Even I wouldn't do that.
variants.elementalist: Fire and wind are with me. Watch out, Shadowhand!
variants.tinker: Bolt, it's going to get dark. Stay close to me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wraith melted away like fog in the sun. The tunnel grew a little brighter.

lines.speaker: shadowhand
lines.text: Did you bring me a little more light? How kind.

lines.speaker: shadowhand
lines.text: The gloom is not evil, little ones. It only waits until all the lights go out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three dark braziers stand along the walls. While they stay unlit, Shadowhand is almost untouchable.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A crack runs across the glass ball on Shadowhand's chest. Golden rays shine through it.

lines.speaker: shadowhand
lines.text: Enough games! Now I will take your light too!

victory.speaker: shadowhand
victory.text: No! Take this glow away!

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The ball shattered, and the stolen light burst out of the cave and into the sky.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: Shadowhand crumbled into a swarm of black butterflies, and they fluttered away into the dark.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: Above the town hall, the Guardian Lantern shone again. The fog retreated all the way to the edge of the forest.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: We did it!

variants.warden: There. Nobody got hurt. Almost.
variants.wind-archer: Not one arrow too many.
variants.herbalist: Everyone's safe? Wonderful.
variants.rogue: Easy. Next time, make it harder, please.
variants.elementalist: Did you see that? Did you see that fire?!
variants.tinker: Everything works. Even me.

victory.speaker: marta
victory.text: The Braveheart Guild lives again. And I'll embroider your names on the banner myself.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Hello, Bravehearts! The fog won't take you. Come back, and we'll try again.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Shadowhand is strong, but the braziers are stronger. Light all three, and he can't hide.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: Get some rest. They say something goes bump in the Gray Mountains at night.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The rumbling from the Grey Mountains carries all the way to the Fat Goose. And on the doorstep stands a girl in a hood far too big for her.

intro.speaker: lina
intro.text: Dad and the miners went to the mine to see what was humming. Three days ago. And nobody came back.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: You heard her, Bravehearts. Take bread for everyone, and some for the miners too.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The tunnel is shorter, but the ceiling there is old. Where it cracks, don't stand. And run for the lift.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Down into the tunnel!

variants.warden: I'll go first. If the ceiling falls, let it fall on my shield.
variants.wind-archer: No wind under the ground. I'll have to listen to the stones.
variants.herbalist: Don't worry, Lina. We'll find your dad.
variants.rogue: Dark, cramped and smells of rats. Almost like home.
variants.elementalist: The ground here hums like a drum. I wonder why?
variants.tinker: Old supports. Bolt, don't touch a single beam.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Something cracked overhead, and sand trickled from the ceiling. The crack shows where the rocks will fall.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ore gallery stretches far into the dark. Black moths watch the party from the walls.

lines.speaker: flip
lines.text: Hey! I'm stuck in the cart! Will you pull me out? I'll give back everything I stole. Well, almost everything.

lines.speaker: rogue
lines.text: A fellow thief? Fine, I'll pull you out. But you're not getting the frying pan.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The moth fluttered and crumbled into grey dust. Just like the ones that flew from Shadowhand.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The party dashed onto the lift, and behind them the gallery came down with a roar.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: In the chest lies Theo's helmet. Someone has scratched one word on it: "Forge".

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The lift rope has been gnawed through, but nearby a path leads down to Copperdale.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: Now to the miners.

variants.warden: I'll carry the helmet. We'll give it back to Theo ourselves.
variants.wind-archer: Chimney smoke down below. Someone's there.
variants.herbalist: The helmet is whole. So Theo is whole too.
variants.rogue: Who writes that on a helmet? Someone who was very scared.
variants.elementalist: A forge under the mountains? I've read about one. A giant worked there.
variants.tinker: That rope was chewed. Small, sharp teeth. Gremlins.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: The ceiling fell, but you're safe, and that's what matters. Rest, then try again.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: No dawdling in the tunnel. Run for the lift and leave the fighting for later.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: Lina is peeling potatoes for me and asks about her dad every minute. Hurry to Copperdale.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Lina told us about a path over the pass. Only goats go that way, her dad used to say.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Well, there are no goats among you. But there is a shepherd heading to Copperdale too. Take him there safely.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: And you, sweetheart, stay here with me. You'll peel potatoes and boss the cat around.

intro.speaker: lina
intro.text: Tell Dad I'm waiting. And that the cat listens to me.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Up to the pass!

variants.warden: The shepherd walks behind me. Anyone who bothers him deals with my shield.
variants.wind-archer: These are my mountains. I know where the wind blows hardest.
variants.herbalist: Thyme grows on the pass. I'll pick some for Marta.
variants.rogue: I'm holding my hat with both hands. I suggest you do the same.
variants.elementalist: Wind! Finally an element I'm on first-name terms with.
variants.tinker: Bolt, hold on to my leg. You'll be the first to blow away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A pole with pennants stands on the ledge. Whichever way they flap, that's where the next gust will blow.

lines.speaker: wind-archer
lines.text: Stay close to the rock. On the edge the wind knocks even goats off their feet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ram shook its head, the fog drifted out of its wool, and it wandered off to graze. The shepherd is delighted: it's his ram.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the old outpost, bandits are sharing out their loot. The lookout is already reaching for his horn.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The shepherd reached the outpost safe and sound. His rams are as gentle as lambs again.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: He gives the party a sack of warm wool. In Alba they'll sew sheepskin coats from it.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: From the outpost you can see Copperdale: the bandits' campfire on the square and purple lanterns by the storehouses.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: Now down to the village.

variants.warden: The shepherd is safe. The miners are next.
variants.wind-archer: I told you: in the mountains you listen to the wind.
variants.herbalist: Purple lanterns? Those are cultists. Theo is there.
variants.rogue: A bandit is muttering about a forge that works by itself. At night. With no smith.
variants.elementalist: A forge without a smith? That's magic! Or a ghost. Or both.
variants.tinker: Warm wool for a cold wind. A fair trade.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: It was the wind that beat you, not the bandits. Rest now, the shepherd will wait.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Stay by the shepherd. He only walks on when one of you is close.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: Lina already bosses the cat better than I do. Now it's the miners' turn.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Copperdale lay asleep under the snow. Only the campfire crackled on the square, and purple hoods walked by the storehouses.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The miners are locked in cages. Knock the locks off all three and let them run home.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Theo must be in the mine office. Lina asked me to tell him she's waiting for him at supper.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Let's open the cages!

variants.warden: We'll open the cages and politely ask the bandits to leave.
variants.wind-archer: I count three cages. And a lot of hoods.
variants.herbalist: The miners are frozen. I brought hot tea for everyone.
variants.rogue: Locks on cages? Oh, that's my favourite.
variants.elementalist: I'll be needing the bandits' campfire. Thank you, bandits.
variants.tinker: These locks are rusty. One good hit and they'll spring open.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The crossbowman by the fire keeps eyeing the bell. If it rings, another brute will come running.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A cage of miners stands in the storehouse. They wave to the party with frozen hands.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.text: Who's there? Bravehearts from Alba? Then Lina found you!

victory.speaker: theo
victory.text: Thank you, Bravehearts. Down below is the Old Forge, and in it Hammerfist, our smith giant.

victory.speaker: theo
victory.text: He slept for a hundred years. Now he forges something black, and the moths fly to him like to a lamp.

victory.speaker: theo
victory.text: Take my lantern. It's dark as a sack down there. I'll leave it at the entrance to the depths.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: Everyone is free!

variants.warden: All the miners are free. Now we can take a breather.
variants.wind-archer: Moths fly to the light. Worth remembering.
variants.herbalist: Theo, drink some tea. And no mines until spring.
variants.rogue: Three locks, three cages. Not one broken finger.
variants.elementalist: A smith giant? I want to see him. From a distance.
variants.tinker: Lovely lantern. Brass, glass, a good wick.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: The cages are still locked, but the miners are holding on. Come back, they're waiting.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Don't fight everyone in sight. Break the cage locks while the bandits stand there gaping.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: Lina threw her arms around her dad's neck and won't let go. She says she knew you'd manage.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The deeper you go, the quieter it gets. At the entrance to the lower tunnels stands Theo's lantern, just as he promised.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Carry the lantern to the forge gate. Whoever gets tired and falls will drop it, so pick it up.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: And remember: in the dark you only see someone who's right next to you.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Stay in the light.

variants.warden: Whoever carries the lantern walks behind me. I'll shield you.
variants.wind-archer: No use shooting into the dark. I'll move closer.
variants.herbalist: It smells of moss and cold water here. Take my arm.
variants.rogue: Finally the dark is on my side. Well, almost.
variants.elementalist: I can light the way with fire. Not for long, but bright.
variants.tinker: I've turned up the lantern's wick so it burns longer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The underground lake is black and still. The water is cold, and wading through it is slow.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Black moths swarm out of the dark toward the lantern's light. The brighter the light, the more of them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two cold braziers stand by the gate. Light them, and the dark will retreat.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The lantern touched the seal, and it blazed up. The heavy doors creaked open.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: From inside comes a boom, boom, boom. And a slow, sleepy voice.

victory.speaker: hammerfist
victory.text: Who brings light? Light must be forged into darkness.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: He's in there.

variants.warden: He's not evil. He's just very tired.
variants.wind-archer: Each boom is slower. The giant is falling asleep on his feet.
variants.herbalist: A voice like a grandpa who hasn't slept all week.
variants.rogue: Forge light into darkness? Sounds like a bad idea.
variants.elementalist: You can't forge light into darkness! Well, that's what the books say.
variants.tinker: Hear how he strikes? A master. A true master.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: The dark outwitted you. Never mind, the lantern is fine. Try again.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Don't run ahead without light. Stay near the lantern and light the braziers.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: A smith who forges darkness? That's not neighbourly. Let's go and have a word.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The foundry is hot and cramped. Further on, in the Furnace Hall, something booms, and the floor shakes.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: While the Dark Lantern is whole, the giant is almost impossible to hurt. And the furnaces call the moths, so smash those too.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: He's no villain, he's been bewitched. Wake him up, don't hurt his feelings.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: To the Furnace!

variants.warden: Stone against the town hall door. Let's see who's tougher.
variants.wind-archer: A lantern on an anvil. One arrow, then another.
variants.herbalist: He's asleep on his feet. We'll wake him gently.
variants.rogue: I wouldn't even steal the Dark Lantern. Just smash it.
variants.elementalist: The furnace is full of fire. And fire listens to me.
variants.tinker: What an anvil! Shame about the bad work on it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Dark Lantern stands on the anvil, and above it towers Hammerfist, made of stone and copper.

lines.speaker: hammerfist
lines.text: Don't disturb me. The Dark Lantern is almost done.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The moth above the furnace turned pale and flew up toward the air shaft.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The furnace in the giant's chest blazed hot, and new moths fluttered out of it.

lines.speaker: hammerfist
lines.text: Hot. Very hot. Keep it down!

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The Dark Lantern shattered, and the black moths turned white. One by one they flew up toward the light of the Guardian Lantern.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The giant sat down on the floor and rubbed his eyes.

victory.speaker: hammerfist
victory.text: Oh. Was I forging at night again? Sorry about the noise.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: He's awake!

variants.warden: No harm done. We make noise at night sometimes too.
variants.wind-archer: The moths are turning white. I told you they weren't evil.
variants.herbalist: Here's some mint tea. It helps you sleep.
variants.rogue: Nice hammer you've got. No, I don't want to borrow it. Well, maybe a little.
variants.elementalist: White moths! I've never seen that, not even in books!
variants.tinker: Will you show me your tools? I'll show you Bolt.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: But one black moth never turned white. It flew north, to where there is more snow than sky.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Hammerfist is as solid as a cliff. Rest, and next time smash the Dark Lantern first.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Don't stand by the furnace, it burns. And smash the furnaces while they're calling moths.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: Now we have a smith giant too. Maybe he can at least make nails for the roof.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Past Thornwood lies the Sleepy Marsh. The mist sits on the water like a blanket on a sleeping cat.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The moths flew off to the marsh, and the mist there is so thick you can’t see your own spoon. Take the boardwalk to the ferryman’s farm.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: And watch out for the Hopper Chief. It’s jumping to the farm too, and whoever gets there first gets the ferry.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Onto the boardwalk!

variants.warden: The boards are narrow and I’m wide. Walk behind me, I’ll check they hold.
variants.wind-archer: Hear the croaking? That’s not a quarrel. They’re counting off.
variants.herbalist: Bog myrtle and cranberries grow in the marsh. Just don’t eat anything without asking me.
variants.rogue: I don’t like wet boots. But I do like a race against a frog.
variants.elementalist: Mist is just water in the air. I read that. It doesn’t scare me. Almost.
variants.tinker: Bolt, keep to the middle of the boards. You swim like a nail.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The boardwalk stretches far into the mist. Deep dark water lies to the left and right, and beside it the Hopper Chief leaps from lily pad to lily pad.

lines.speaker: wind-archer
lines.text: The frogs jump on the third step. Count it: one, two, hop. And don’t stand where they land.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Suddenly the mist stirs, as if someone smoothed it with a hand.

lines.speaker: mist-queen
lines.text: Shhh. The marsh is sleeping. Who’s that splashing along my boardwalk?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Marsh Hopper gave a funny hiccup, the mist flew off its back, and it plopped into the water to catch gnats.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Here is the ferryman’s farm. Grey wolves stand by the ferry, with the same mist in their eyes.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The party reached the farm first. The Hopper Chief sat on a stump and puffed out its cheeks in a sulk.

victory.speaker: ferryman
victory.text: Thank you, Brave Ones. This mist isn’t ordinary. Someone weaves it at night on old looms, thread by thread.

victory.speaker: ferryman
victory.text: And Old Heron is all alone on her island. The mist has crept up to her hut, and she can’t see her boat.

victory.speaker: ferryman
victory.text: And at the forest pond the moths are putting out the fireflies, one by one. Where will you go first?

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: We have to choose.

variants.warden: Someone needs a shield and someone needs a light. You choose, I’ll follow.
variants.wind-archer: Herons don’t like being frightened. Neither do fireflies.
variants.herbalist: Old Heron? My Heron? She taught me everything I know.
variants.rogue: Someone weaves mist? I wonder what a loom like that is worth.
variants.elementalist: Fireflies glow without any heat. I’ve always wanted to see that.
variants.tinker: Looms in a marsh? The wood will swell. Strange work.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: The frog was quicker. Never mind, dry your boots and we’ll try again.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Keep away from deep water, your feet get stuck there. And ring the bell on the little island. It calls the ferry.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: The ferryman sent a basket of cranberries. Now choose: Old Heron or the fireflies?

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Old Heron’s island sits in the middle of the marsh. A hut on tall stilts, a herb garden all around, and thick mist.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Old Heron is slow and her eyes are weak. Walk her to the boat at the pier and stay close.

intro.speaker: herbalist
intro.text: She’s the one who taught me! Any moment now she’ll ask if I label my jars. She always asks.

intro.speaker: heron
intro.text: Who’s that stomping through my garden? Oh, the Brave Ones. Well, lead the way, but not too fast.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Stay close to Old Heron.

variants.warden: Take my arm, Granny. I’m slow too, so we’re a good match.
variants.wind-archer: Herons stand on one leg and never hurry. This one doesn’t either.
variants.herbalist: Your mint has grown right up to the gate. I’ll pick a little, all right?
variants.rogue: So many jars! No, I won’t take any. I’m just counting.
variants.elementalist: The mist in the reeds is like a wall. A little wind and it’ll clear.
variants.tinker: The hut’s stilts are leaning. When we’re back I’ll fix them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mint, chamomile and St John’s wort grow in the garden. And thornlings are stirring among them.

lines.speaker: heron
lines.text: Careful with the chamomile! Oh, no, that’s not chamomile. That’s a thornling.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The reeds sink into white banks of mist. You can’t see through them, you only hear rustling.

lines.speaker: heron
lines.text: I don’t go into the mist. Long ago I pulled a little boy out of it. I still remember how he shivered.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Cultists wait by the boat, and one is already puffing his cheeks and raising a horn.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: Old Heron sat down in the boat and straightened her headscarf. The mist around the island grew thinner.

victory.speaker: heron
victory.text: That boy from the mist had a little lantern. It went out, and he sat on a tussock in the dark until morning.

victory.speaker: heron
victory.text: I gave him a candle, and he said: when I grow up, I’ll make a lantern that never goes out. His name was Lumo.

victory.speaker: herbalist
victory.text: She just asked if I still don’t label my jars. I pretended not to hear.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: Lumo was afraid of the dark.

variants.warden: So that’s where his fear comes from. A dark night in the marsh with no one beside him.
variants.wind-archer: Animals in the dark aren’t scary. But a little one doesn’t know that.
variants.herbalist: That’s Old Heron all over: first she rescues you, then she makes you tea.
variants.rogue: A lantern that never goes out. Well, he kept his promise.
variants.elementalist: Shadowhand was little and scared once too. They don’t put that in books.
variants.tinker: A boy who dreamed of a lantern. When I was small, I dreamed of gears.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Old Heron got tired and sat down to rest. Never mind, she’ll wait while you get your strength back.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Clear the mist with fire or wind before Old Heron steps into it. Someone is hiding in there.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: Old Heron sent me her tea and a pair of boots. She says you can’t take a step in the marsh without them.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: In the woods beyond the marsh lies a quiet pond. Every night fireflies dance over it, as if someone had scattered sparks.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: But tonight black cocoons hang over the water, and moths are crawling out of them. Only eight fireflies are left.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Keep the moths away from the pond and break the cocoons. Let at least one firefly see the morning.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Protect the fireflies!

variants.warden: I’ll stand by the water. Let the moths try to get past me first.
variants.wind-archer: Three paths lead to the pond. I’m watching all three.
variants.herbalist: Fireflies like damp grass. Please don’t trample the bank.
variants.rogue: You can’t steal a firefly. It decides who to glow for.
variants.elementalist: The night breeze comes off the water. I’ll try to turn it on the cocoons.
variants.tinker: Bolt, no barking. The fireflies are scared enough already.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: New moths fly in from the east. The fireflies huddle in the middle of the pond.

lines.speaker: elementalist
lines.text: The book said fireflies make cold light. I didn’t believe it. Now I can see it.

lines.speaker: mist-queen
lines.text: Why do you need these little lights? It’s so quiet and dark without them. No one will see a thing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The moth turned pale, circled over the water and settled on a reed next to a firefly.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: Morning came. The fireflies rose over the pond and formed a picture, as if they were drawing with light.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: In the picture is a boy with a glass jar. He’s catching fireflies so he won’t be afraid of the night.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: And in the morning he opens the jar and lets them go. The fireflies remember his name: Lumo.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: Later he grew up and made a lantern. Its very first lights were fireflies from this pond.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: He let them go.

variants.warden: He was afraid of the dark and still let the fireflies go. A good heart.
variants.wind-archer: Whoever lets a creature go understands it. Lumo understood.
variants.herbalist: Poor little thing. He just needed someone to sit with him at night.
variants.rogue: Alba’s lantern started with fireflies in a jar? What a story.
variants.elementalist: Cold light that never goes out. That’s why the Guardian Lantern never feels warm.
variants.tinker: A jar, a lid, air holes. That’s how every good lantern begins.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: The moths put out all the fireflies. Don’t be sad, they’re only asleep, and we’ll come back tomorrow night.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Stand on the paths, not right by the water. And break the cocoons first, because new moths keep coming out of them.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: One firefly followed you all the way to the inn. Now it sits in a jar on the shelf and glows for the cat.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The bell-ringer’s map led to an old bell tower. It stands waist-deep in water, and three bells still hang at the very top.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Long ago the bell-ringer rang into the mist so lost folk could find their way home. The map shows the order.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Ring the bells in the right order and the hatch to the roof will open. But don’t dawdle: the water is rising.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Up to the bells!

variants.warden: I know how to ring bells. At the town hall I woke the whole square every morning.
variants.wind-archer: Hear that? The wind brushes the bells and they hum ever so softly.
variants.herbalist: The water’s cold. Whoever gets wet gets hot linden tea afterwards.
variants.rogue: Bell-ringer, map, treasure. I can feel there’s treasure here somewhere.
variants.elementalist: Sound travels through the air too. So bells are almost my element.
variants.tinker: I’ll look at the clappers. A hundred years without oil, poor things.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the belfry three bells stand in a circle. The wall shows the same picture as the map.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Splash. The water in the porch has risen one step higher.

lines.speaker: mist-queen
lines.text: Don’t ring. Please. You’ll wake the whole marsh and the mist will lift.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The hatch swung open and fresh air rushed across the roof. Beside the weathervane stands the bell-ringer’s chest.

lines.speaker: rogue
lines.text: The bell-ringer’s treasure! He’d say so himself: take it if you ring true.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The party is on the roof. The bells are still humming, and the sound rolls far across the marsh.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: Somewhere deep in the mist something cracked. One of the Queen’s looms broke and fell silent.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: The marsh is awake.

variants.warden: A fine peal. Like the town hall before the fair.
variants.wind-archer: The herons took off and the frogs went quiet. The whole marsh is listening.
variants.herbalist: Now no lost soul will sit alone in the mist all night.
variants.rogue: Rung fair, taken fair. The bell-ringer would be pleased.
variants.elementalist: Sound clears the mist! They definitely didn’t teach me that at the academy.
variants.tinker: I oiled the clappers, and the bells knew the rest.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: The water was faster. Never mind, we’ll dry off by the stove and try again.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Check the picture on the wall before you ring. A wrong bell wakes the slimes and starts it all over.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: I hung the bell-ringer’s little bell over the door. Whoever comes in rings it, and the cat runs to say hello.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: At the very heart of the marsh stands an avenue of willows. Beyond it comes a soft clatter: click-clack, click-clack, as if someone were weaving.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The Mist Queen is in there. While her looms stand, arrows and spells barely reach her. Break the looms.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: And remember: she’s one of Lumo’s moths too. Set her free and maybe she’ll tell you something.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: To the Heart of the Mist!

variants.warden: The mist isn’t afraid of a shield. But the shield isn’t afraid of the mist either.
variants.wind-archer: A big moth flies slowly. I’ll wait for the mist to part.
variants.herbalist: I brought mint. It always helps anyone who hasn’t slept for a long time.
variants.rogue: A loom that weaves mist. A shame to break, hard to steal. I’ll break it.
variants.elementalist: Wind against mist. A fair duel at last.
variants.tinker: I’ve only ever fixed one loom. Breaking it will be easier.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A huge pale moth hovers in the middle of the hall. Around her, looms clatter away, weaving mist.

lines.speaker: mist-queen
lines.text: Shhh. Don’t disturb me. A little more mist and no one will see a thing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A little moth turned pale and settled on the Queen’s wing. She shivered, as if remembering something.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Queen tugged her last thread, and new moths fluttered out of the mist.

lines.speaker: mist-queen
lines.text: Don’t lift the mist! He’s under it. He doesn’t want to be seen.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The last loom fell silent. The mist sank onto the water and melted away, and the Queen turned white as milk.

victory.speaker: mist-queen
victory.text: I was Lumo’s very first moth. I wove mist so no one would see him taking other people’s light.

victory.speaker: mist-queen
victory.text: Look. I’ll show you the night it all began.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: A picture appears in the mist. People from Alba are carrying the Guardian Lantern to the town hall, to light the whole city.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: And Lumo is left alone in the dark workshop. His candle has burned down, and he’s scared again, just like that night in the marsh.

victory.speaker: herbalist
victory.text: Here, Your Majesty, some mint tea. Just like I made for Bruno. It helps you sleep without any mist.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: He was just scared.

variants.warden: He gave his light to everyone and kept none for himself. I’d be sad too.
variants.wind-archer: A frightened animal hides and bites. A frightened person too, it seems.
variants.herbalist: There’s no herb for fear. Only someone beside you and a candle on the table.
variants.rogue: He stole light because they took his own. That I understand.
variants.elementalist: Shadowhand isn’t an evil wizard. He’s a boy who’s still in the dark.
variants.tinker: A craftsman made something for everyone and was left with nothing. That’s not right.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The Queen spread her white wings. But black moths rose over the marsh and flew west, to the Shadow Tower near Alba.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The mist creeps slowly after them. It’s heading for the city.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: The Queen hid in her mist. Rest up, and next time break the looms first.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Every loom calls a moth and heals the Queen. Clear the mist with fire or wind so you can see her.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: The mist is coming for Alba. Shut the shutters, Brave Ones, and I’ll put on my biggest pot of soup. We’ll defend the town together.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: East of Alba, up in the mountains, lies Glass Town. A crystal road leads there, sparkling in the sun like a frozen stream.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The second flock of moths flew that way. Master Ida, an old lamplighter, is waiting for you at the coaching yard. She’s taking her cart up to the town gate.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The cart is heavy and Ida walks slowly. Keep her safe, and don’t break the mirrors along the road. They’re not there just for show.

intro.speaker: ida
intro.text: You’re the Brave Ones? Good. Don’t push the cart, there’s glass in it. I may be slow, but I don’t like waiting.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: To the gate!

variants.warden: The road is slippery as ice. I’ll go first, you stay behind my shield.
variants.wind-archer: Mirrors all along the road. I wonder who looks into them when we’re not here.
variants.herbalist: Mistress Ida, your hands are cold. Take these gloves, I’ve got a spare pair.
variants.rogue: A whole cart full of glass. I’m not touching it. See? Hands in my pockets.
variants.elementalist: Crystal loves earth and mirrors love light. This place is made for magic!
variants.tinker: The cart wheels squeak. Bolt, remind me to oil them when we stop.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The crystal road glitters, and every mirror along the roadside holds a piece of sky.

lines.speaker: ida
lines.text: Don’t break the mirrors. My apprentice put them up long ago, so the road would never be dark at night.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: All the mirrors flashed at once, and black moths fluttered out of the farthest ones.

lines.speaker: glass-guardian
lines.text: Ding. Who goes to the workshop? The master is not at home. The master will be back soon.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The bridge sways over the gorge, and one of the cart’s wheels is stuck between the planks.

lines.speaker: warden
lines.text: Let me. The town hall doors are heavier, and I opened them every morning.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Cultists stand by the gate of Glass Town, their eyes hidden under their hoods.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The cart rolled through the gate. Glass Town chimed with a thousand windowpanes, as if saying hello.

victory.speaker: ida
victory.text: Thank you, Brave Ones. Forty years ago the Guardian Lantern was carried down this very road to Alba. My best apprentice made it. His name was Lumo.

victory.speaker: ida
victory.text: He came to me as a little boy, with a jar of fireflies under his arm. And every night he left a candle burning on his workbench.

victory.speaker: ida
victory.text: His workshop still stands on the hill, and his notes are kept in the Library of Light. Where will you go first?

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: We have to choose.

variants.warden: Workshop or books? I’ll go wherever something needs carrying.
variants.wind-archer: The workshop smells of iron, the library of dust. My nose votes for the workshop.
variants.herbalist: A boy who never blew out his candle. Poor thing, he can’t have slept a wink.
variants.rogue: A lamplighter’s workshop. Must be full of interesting bits and bobs. I’ll just have a look.
variants.elementalist: The Library of Light! They say the books there whisper. Oh. That’s right next to my academy.
variants.tinker: The workshop where the Guardian Lantern was made? I’ve dreamed of seeing it since I was little.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Ida got tired and the cart had to stop. Never mind, have a rest and set off again.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Stand between Ida and the enemies. And no area attacks near the mirrors: a cracked mirror can’t help you any more.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: Ida left me a little glass ball. Give it a shake, and snow falls over a tiny town inside.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Lumo’s workshop stands on the hill above Glass Town. Downstairs is a glassworks with two furnaces, and his drawings still lie up in the attic.

intro.speaker: ida
intro.text: This is where he worked. I haven’t been inside for forty years. The Lantern drawing is in the attic. Bring it out before the moths get their little feet on it.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The drawing is big, and whoever carries it walks slower. If you get tired, put it down and let someone else pick it up.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Into the workshop!

variants.warden: The furnaces are still warm. Someone’s been keeping house here without the master.
variants.wind-archer: Hear that? Ticking. Something in the storeroom ticks like a heart.
variants.herbalist: So much dust! Whoever sneezes gets chamomile. Whoever doesn’t, gets some too.
variants.rogue: A workshop full of knick-knacks and nobody saying “don’t touch”. Almost paradise.
variants.elementalist: Glass is blown with fire. I can do fire. Glass, not yet.
variants.tinker: Bolt, this is Lumo’s own workshop. Wipe your paws. Both of them. No, all four.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Brass automatons stand in the storeroom, ticking softly in their sleep. Each has a winding key in its side.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: Clean gears, not a speck of rust. Someone loved him. Bolt, stop growling, you’re a good boy too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A soft glassy chime drifts down from the attic, as if someone had tapped a goblet.

lines.speaker: glass-guardian
lines.text: Ding. Do not touch the drawings. The master will be back soon, and he will be sad.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Under the roof stands a workbench. On it lie the Lantern drawing and a little candle burned right down to its saucer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The automaton clicked, the key in its side stopped turning, and it sat down on the floor like a tired puppy.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The drawing is at the door. The party unrolls it on the floor, and Ida bends over it.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: There is the Guardian Lantern, every gear and every pane. And in the margin, a little sketch: a crystal automaton with a heart like a tiny lamp.

victory.speaker: ida
victory.text: That’s the Guardian. Lumo built him as a helper, so the workshop wouldn’t be lonely. I thought he was long gone.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: Under the sketch, in Lumo’s hand, it says: “Light for everyone. And a little for me.”

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: A little for himself.

variants.warden: A little light for himself. Is that so much? No. Not at all.
variants.wind-archer: An animal digs its burrow for itself. Lumo built for everyone.
variants.herbalist: Someone who looks after everyone needs someone to look after them.
variants.rogue: “A little for me.” You know, I understand that better than I’d like to.
variants.elementalist: So many formulas! I’m copying them. Just don’t call it cheating.
variants.tinker: I’ve never seen a drawing like this. Bolt and I will build something good from it, I promise.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: The drawing is still in the attic. Never mind, it’s waited forty years, it can wait one more day.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Pass the drawing along before its carrier gets worn out. And turn the keys in the storeroom: a brass helper is handy in a fight.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: The drawing is spread out on my table. Now I chop onions on one end, because the Lantern is on the other.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The Library of Light stands next to the academy. By day the sun pours in through tall windows, and at night the books on the shelves whisper.

intro.speaker: ida
intro.text: Lumo’s notes are in the reading room, in an old diary. But go quietly: the living books hate noise and call the guards at once.

intro.speaker: elementalist
intro.text: This is my academy’s library. Just don’t tell the librarian I’m here. I still owe her three books.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Quietly now, on tiptoe.

variants.warden: I’m quiet. Well, my armour isn’t, but I am.
variants.wind-archer: Walk like a fox on snow. Heel first, then toes.
variants.herbalist: It smells of dust and old glue in here. If you need to sneeze, sneeze into your sleeve.
variants.rogue: Sneaking I can do. At last it’s for a good cause.
variants.elementalist: I know every shelf here. Well, almost every one. Well, the ones near the exit.
variants.tinker: Bolt, not one bark. Not one. Not even a whisper of one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A long hall of shelves. The books stir their pages and mumble in their sleep, and ghosts doze between the shelves.

lines.speaker: glass-guardian
lines.text: Ding. Who goes to the master’s diary? It is not yours. The master will be back soon.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A cold draught blows through the gallery windows. Pages rustle, as if the wind were turning them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the reading room table lies a thick diary with a little lantern drawn on the cover.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The party is at the table. Ida opens the diary, and dust rises from it, light as snowflakes.

victory.speaker: ida
victory.text: That’s Lumo’s handwriting. Listen.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: “Today they took the Guardian Lantern to Alba. Everyone sang and cheered. I cheered too. But in the evening the workshop got very dark.”

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: “The Guardian asks why I don’t light a candle. I told him I gave all my lights to the Lantern. I’m scared.”

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: He was scared.

variants.warden: He gave all his light to the town and kept none. I’d have sat with him that evening.
variants.wind-archer: Owls aren’t afraid of the night, because they can see in it. Lumo couldn’t see a thing.
variants.herbalist: Someone should have dropped by with a cup of hot tea. Nobody did.
variants.rogue: I know what that’s like: alone in the dark, and no one knocks. Read on.
variants.elementalist: One day we’ll give this diary back to him. Let him read for himself that he isn’t bad.
variants.tinker: He put his own lights in the Lantern instead of keeping them. Makers often do that, and then they’re sad.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: The books made such a racket that you were shown the door. Never mind, the books will fall asleep again, and you can try once more.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Don’t stop next to the living shelves, or the books wake up. Tiptoe and keep to the middle of the hall.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: I’ve locked the diary away in a chest. It ought to go back to its owner, and I have a feeling we’ll meet him yet.
